ring_sizing.standard: ISO 8653 sizes a ring by its inner circumference in millimetres; EU sizes are that circumference; one full US size ≈ 2.55 mm of circumference (≈0.81 mm of diameter).
rules: Bands wider than 6 mm fit tighter: recommend half a size up.
Comfort-fit band thickness 1.5–2.0 mm; flat band 1.2–1.5 mm minimum for engraving.
Outer-band text height ≈ 60–70 % of band width; a phrase line needs a band ≥ 5 mm; an inner engraving needs ≥ 3 mm band and ≥ 1.2 mm thickness.
Usable engraving length on the outside ≈ 80 % of the circumference; on the inside ≈ 60 % (leave the size stamp and hallmark area).
Cut-out name pendants: 0.8–1.2 mm sheet (1.0 mm standard women's, 1.2–1.5 mm men's / statement / bracelet plates).

Minimum stroke, gap and bridge come from materials.json + the workshop profile (e.g. silver-925 min stroke 0.6 mm, min bridge 0.8 mm) — the platform's manufacturing gate enforces them; these numbers are not to be relaxed by the copilot.
Every closed counter (ه م و ص ف ق ة) is an island unless bridged; dots < 0.8 mm diameter are dropped from cut-out geometry only with explicit customer confirmation.
Polishing removes ≈ 0.05 mm per side; plating adds ≈ 0.003 mm — the outline is exported nominal, allowances live in the profile.
Integrated ring holes on a cut-out piece: ≥ 1.2 mm inner diameter with ≥ 0.8 mm wall so a 0.8–1.0 mm jump ring passes.
Jump rings: 0.8–1.0 mm wire, 3–4 mm inner diameter for pendants; soldered closed for anything that carries a chain.
Bails should be ≥ 1.5 × the chain width; a fixed top loop sits on the vertical centre of gravity or the piece tilts.
Lobster clasps 9–12 mm (women), 12–16 mm (men); spring rings 5–6 mm; extender chain 3–5 cm with a drop tag.
Cufflink faces 15–18 mm on a soldered post/toggle; a solid 4 mm pad is reserved on the reverse centre.
Brooch bar pins: pin wire 0.8–1.0 mm, catch on the reverse of the structural bar, never on a letter.
Keychain discs 25–35 mm with a top ring ≥ 2 mm inner diameter for a split ring.
Women's name necklaces: cable chain 1.0–1.5 mm, 40–45 cm (+5 cm extender); kids 35–38 cm; men 55–65 cm with 2–6 mm curb/rope.
Bracelet chain: 16–21 cm total (wrist + 1–2 cm), name plate 25–35 mm wide; men's bracelets 21 cm per the owner's chain catalogue.
Lariat / Y drop 5–8 cm below the collarbone; station necklaces keep stations ≥ 4 cm apart or they stack.
Chain weight is added to the plate weight when quoting; the owner's stated per-length weights are in wearability.json.
A stone that replaces a dot: 1.5–2.0 mm, prong or bezel seat = stone diameter + 0.6 mm; the stroke is widened locally to ≥ 2.6 mm around the seat.
Bezel wall 0.3–0.4 mm, at least 0.5 mm of metal around any stone; pavé uses 1.0–1.5 mm stones with ≈ 0.3 mm spacing and needs ≥ 1.2 mm plate thickness.
Pearls as chain stations 3–4 mm (freshwater), drops 6–8 mm; drilled pearls are chain parts, never cut geometry.
Coloured glass beads (evil eye, turquoise) are threaded stations or capped drops — a BOM item with a ring, not part of the outline.
Enamel needs closed cells: wall ≥ 0.4 mm (cold/resin enamel) or ≥ 0.6 mm (vitreous), recess 0.3–0.5 mm deep.
Colour is a finishing instruction; only cell walls are cut geometry (materials.json marks enamel as visual-preview-only for weight).
Gulf customers commonly buy 21K and 18K gold; 925 silver (plain, gold-plated or rhodium-plated) is the everyday personalised line.

UAE: precious-metal articles are expected to carry a fineness stamp / hallmark — reserve a flat ≥ 3 × 1.5 mm area on the reverse (or inside a ring band) for the stamp; confirm the current UAE rule with MoIAT / Dubai Central Laboratory before claiming compliance.
Gold plating: flash < 0.5 µm, standard 1–2.5 µm; 'vermeil' means ≥ 2.5 µm gold over sterling (US FTC definition) — do not use the word otherwise.
White gold is rhodium-plated 0.5–1 µm; polishing allowance and plating allowance are already in materials.json.
metals_fineness_and_marking.weight_formula: grams = area_mm2 × thickness_mm × density_g_cm3 / 1000 (the platform's weight report computes this from the real outline)

rules: Earrings: ≤ 2 g each for studs, ≤ 5 g for drops; post 0.8 mm × 10 mm.
A dainty name reads best at 30–35 mm wide × 1.0 mm thick; men's pieces go to 45 mm and 1.5 mm.
Kids: bold rounded lettering, stroke ≥ 1.0 mm, no free-hanging hairlines.
Laser engraving: Latin text ≥ 1.0–1.5 mm cap height; Arabic ≥ 2.0 mm x-height so dots and teeth stay legible; line width ≈ 0.1–0.15 mm, depth 0.05–0.1 mm (hand engraving 0.2–0.3 mm).
Engraved text is never subject to cut-out connectivity rules, but it is still exact-text: the confirmed source text, shaping and order are locked exactly like a cut-out design.
Dates and short phrases go on discs and bar plates; a solid engraved disc can carry far denser text than a pierced plate of the same size.
Source text is customer-confirmed Unicode, never read from a photo; shaping via HarfBuzz; identity is verified letter-by-letter before export.
Dots are structural islands: bridge to the body (preferred), fill into a plate, or replace one dot with a stone — every option is shown before/after and confirmed.
Harakat are optional ornament; dropping or keeping them is a customer decision recorded in the brief; sacred text keeps them exactly as in the canonical source.
Names ending in a low letter (ي ى ن) get the right-hand ring on a raised terminal stroke; multi-name and station layouts lock the reading order in the version hash.

requests.route: exact-text-replacement → keep construction + attachment, regenerate letterforms for the confirmed text, re-run the gate
thin naskh/diwani name, one 1.5–2.0 mm prong seat replacing a dot, stroke widened locally
heart-joined pair, layered 2–3 chain set, or station necklace with reading order locked
cut-out name over an engraved disc (sacred text → enhanced verification) or engraved date line
bold rounded script, stroke ≥ 1.0 mm, 35–38 cm chain or 14–16 cm bracelet, crown/heart/enamel accents at the ends
relief on a darkened disc (dense text allowed) or engraved band; no cut-out hairlines
stacked plates with centre-line rings; a brand logo request is an IP risk → inspired plain medallion instead
style-inspired-redesign only: extract DNA, never geometry; flag copyright/brand risk; offer inspired alternatives
